cards.front: What does Anthropic's documentation call the single most important factor in tool performance?
cards.back: The tool **description**. It is the main signal Claude uses to choose a tool. Aim for at least 3-4 sentences.

cards.front: List the elements of a strong tool description.
cards.back: Purpose; when to use it; when NOT to use it (naming the similar tool); meaning and format of each input; example queries; edge cases/limits; what it returns.

cards.front: Two tools have one-line descriptions and the agent calls the wrong one. What is the best first step?
cards.back: Expand both descriptions with input formats, example queries, edge cases and boundaries versus the other tool. Few-shot examples, routing layers and consolidation come later or are over-engineered.

cards.front: How can a system prompt cause tool misrouting even when descriptions are good?
cards.back: Keyword-sensitive instructions (e.g. "always check the customer record") create unintended associations between many requests and one tool. Review and make such lines conditional.

cards.front: What is the fix for two tools with overlapping names like analyze_content and analyze_document?
cards.back: Rename and re-describe to encode the difference, e.g. analyze_content -> extract_web_results with a web-specific description.

cards.front: How do you fix a vague, do-everything tool like analyze_document?
cards.back: Split it into purpose-specific tools with clear input/output contracts, e.g. extract_data_points, summarize_content, verify_claim_against_source.

cards.front: Why avoid 1:1 API endpoint wrappers as tools?
cards.back: They force many calls for one task (more tokens, more failure points). Prefer task-level tools such as schedule_event over list_users + list_events + create_event.

cards.front: What regex must a Claude API tool name match?
What is input_examples on a tool definition?
cards.back: Optional example inputs that must validate against the input schema (invalid examples cause a 400). Roughly 20-50 tokens each for simple tools, 100-200 for complex ones.

cards.front: What are MCP's two error channels?
cards.back: 1) JSON-RPC protocol errors (unknown tool, invalid params such as -32602). 2) Tool execution errors returned in the result with **isError: true**, so the model sees and reacts to them.

cards.front: Name the four error categories for tool failures.
cards.back: Transient (timeout, service down), validation (bad input), business (policy violation), permission (no access).

cards.front: Which structured fields should a tool error include?
cards.back: errorCategory, isRetryable (boolean; the exam guide also writes it as retriable) and a human-readable description; for business-rule violations, isRetryable: false plus a customer-friendly explanation. These are exam-guide conventions: the MCP spec itself defines only isError.

cards.front: Why is a generic "Operation failed" error harmful?
cards.back: The agent can't tell transient from permanent failures, so it wastes retries or gives up on recoverable work.

cards.front: A search tool times out. Should it return an empty result marked as success?
cards.back: No. That's an access failure and must be reported as an error (isError, category, retryable). An empty success means "the query ran and found no matches".

cards.front: How should a subagent handle a transient failure?
cards.back: Recover locally first (retry/alternative). Propagate to the coordinator only what it can't resolve, with failure type, attempted query, partial results and what it tried.

cards.front: On the Claude API, how do you report a failed client tool call?
cards.back: Return a tool_result with "is_error": true and content explaining what went wrong and what to try next (e.g. "Rate limit exceeded. Retry after 60 seconds.").

cards.front: What happens to tool selection when an agent has 18 tools instead of 4-5?
cards.back: Selection becomes less reliable: more options and more similar descriptions to choose between, plus more context used.

cards.front: A synthesis agent keeps running web searches. Best fix?
cards.back: Remove web search from its tool set (scope tools to the role). Prompt warnings are not a reliable fix.

cards.front: What does replacing fetch_url with load_document illustrate?
cards.back: Constraining a generic tool to what the role needs: load_document validates that the URL is a document, preventing arbitrary fetching.

cards.front: Synthesis needs many simple fact-checks and a few deep ones. Best design?
cards.back: Give synthesis a scoped verify_fact tool for simple checks; route complex verifications through the coordinator to the search agent.

cards.front: tool_choice auto vs any vs tool vs none?
cards.back: auto: Claude may call a tool or answer (default with tools). any: must call some tool. {"type":"tool","name":X}: must call X. none: no tools.

cards.front: How do you guarantee extract_metadata runs before enrichment tools?
cards.back: Force it with tool_choice {"type":"tool","name":"extract_metadata"} on the first turn, then continue later steps in follow-up turns (e.g. with auto).

cards.front: When is tool_choice any the right choice?
cards.back: When you need a guaranteed tool call (structured output) rather than conversational text, but the right tool/schema isn't known in advance.

cards.front: Can Claude write explanatory text before the tool call when tool_choice is any or a forced tool?
cards.back: No. The API prefills the response, so it goes straight to tool_use. Use auto if you want text plus a tool call.

cards.front: In MCP, which side controls tools, resources and prompts?
cards.back: Tools: model-controlled. Resources: application-controlled. Prompts: user-controlled (in Claude Code, slash commands named /mcp__<server>__<prompt>).

cards.front: Why expose a database schema or issue catalog as an MCP resource?
cards.back: It shows the agent what data exists up front, avoiding exploratory tool calls.

cards.front: Host, client, server: what's the relationship?
cards.back: The host (AI app) creates one client per server; each client holds a 1:1 stateful session with its server. JSON-RPC 2.0 with capability negotiation.

cards.front: What is MCP sampling?
cards.back: A server asks the **client's** model to generate a completion, so the server needs no model API key; humans should be able to review it.

cards.front: What's the rule for logging in a stdio MCP server?
cards.back: stdout may carry only MCP messages; send logs to stderr. Printing to stdout corrupts the protocol.

cards.front: Which MCP remote transport is current and which is deprecated?
cards.back: Streamable HTTP is current; the older HTTP+SSE transport is deprecated.

cards.front: Where do you configure an MCP server the whole team should use in Claude Code?
cards.back: Project scope: .mcp.json at the repo root, committed to git (claude mcp add --scope project ...).

cards.front: Where do personal or experimental MCP servers go?
cards.back: User scope in ~/.claude.json (available in all your projects). The default local scope is also stored in ~/.claude.json, for one project.

cards.front: How do you keep tokens out of a committed .mcp.json?
cards.back: Use environment variable expansion: ${GITHUB_TOKEN} or ${VAR:-default}, in command, args, env, url or headers.

cards.front: If user-scope and project-scope servers are both configured, which tools can Claude use?
cards.back: All of them: tools from every configured server are discovered at connection time and available simultaneously.

cards.front: Claude keeps using Grep instead of a more capable MCP search tool. First fix?
cards.back: Enhance the MCP tool's description to explain its capabilities, outputs and when to prefer it over built-in search.

cards.front: Build a custom MCP server for Jira, or use an existing one?
cards.back: Use an existing community/vendor server for standard integrations; reserve custom servers for team-specific workflows.

cards.front: Glob vs Grep?
cards.back: Glob matches file **paths/names** (e.g. **/*.test.tsx). Grep searches file **contents** (callers, error strings, imports).

cards.front: Edit fails because the anchor text appears several times. What now?
cards.back: Use a longer unique anchor (or replace_all if all should change); otherwise Read the full file and Write the corrected version.

cards.front: How should Claude explore an unfamiliar codebase?
cards.back: Incrementally: Grep for entry points, Read those files, follow imports. Don't read every file up front.

cards.front: How do you find every use of a function that wrapper modules re-export under other names?
cards.back: First list all exported names (including aliases/re-exports), then Grep for each name across the codebase.

cards.front: A teammate clones a repo that has a committed .mcp.json. What happens the first time they run Claude Code?
cards.back: Claude Code asks them to approve the project-scoped servers before using them (a committed file could launch arbitrary commands). They also need to set any ${VAR} secrets the file references in their own environment.

cards.front: Version note: are Grep and Glob always in Claude Code's default tool set?
cards.back: Not in current docs: on macOS, Linux and WSL they are absent by default and Claude searches with find/grep through Bash; they return if named in --tools/--allowedTools or in a subagent's tools list without Bash. The exam still treats them as distinct tools: Glob = file names, Grep = file contents.
